title: Infrastructure at an Inflection Point: AI, Power Demand and the Next Phase of Global Growth
summary: This article outlines: Key Takeaways from GCM Grosvenor’s Annual Infrastructure Investor Day
body_text: Key Takeaways from GCM Grosvenor’s Annual Infrastructure Investor Day Infrastructure is entering a new phase of global expansion as artificial intelligence, electrification and industrial modernization require extraordinary expenditure to meet rapidly accelerating demand. At GCM Grosvenor’s annual Infrastructure Investor Day in London, investors and industry partners gathered to discuss the evolving market backdrop and the implications for infrastructure investing over the coming decade. Chief Investment Officer Fred Pollock outlined a constructive — though increasingly selective — outlook for the asset class. While macro uncertainty, higher financing costs and geopolitical volatility require careful consideration, the outlook for infrastructure investments remains supported by the same critical characteristics that have supported infrastructure for decades – durable demand, high barriers to entry, structural capital shortfalls and growing physical constraints tied to power, connectivity and permitting. Markets Are Repricing Expectations, Not Retreating From Risk Markets continue to adjust to a materially different interest rate environment than investors enjoyed for over a decade, post GFC. Expectations for more aggressive monetary easing have given way to a “higher-for-longer” outlook as economic activity continues to demonstrate resilience despite persistent inflation. At the same time, geopolitical tensions and evolving trade dynamics have contributed to greater dispersion across sectors, financing markets and regional economies. While headline equity indices have remained relatively resilient, underlying volatility across asset classes has increased meaningfully. Pollock noted that investor expectations surrounding the long-term cost of capital have shifted considerably over the past year, contributing to repeated repricing across both public and private markets. Against that backdrop, market performance has become increasingly uneven beneath the surface. Sector leadership has narrowed, rate expectations have repeatedly reset, and investors have become more selective. YTD Market Performance Source: Bloomberg Finance, L.P. Performance shown as of April 21, 2026. Long Term Bonds: Bloomberg S. Treasury 20+ Year Total Return Index Aggregate Bond Index: Bloomberg Global-Aggregate Total Return Index Value Unhedged S. High Yield: Bloomberg US Corporate High Yield Total Return Index Value Unhedged Emerging Market Bonds: P. Morgan EMBI Global Diversified Index Past performance is not necessarily indicative of future results. No assurance can be given that any investment will achieve its objectives or avoid losses.For illustrative purposes only. Importantly, periods of heightened uncertainty have not yet translated into broad-based market dislocation. Financing conditions for high-quality assets remain constructive, particularly across sectors supported by durable cash flows and long-term secular demand. That resilience has extended into portions of the infrastructure market, where significant capital needs continue to intersect with rising demand for energy, digital connectivity and industrial modernization. Pollock emphasized that the current environment increasingly reflects a transition away from a broadly beta-driven market toward one characterized by greater dispersion, underwriting selectivity, and differentiated execution capability. Evolving Market Backdrop Source: Bloomberg Finance, L.P. Data as of March 31, 2026. For illustrative purposes only. AI Is Driving One of the Largest Capital Spending Cycles in Modern History One of the most significant themes discussed during the event was the scale of the global AI investment cycle now underway and its implications for infrastructure markets. Pollock noted that hyperscaler capital expenditures continue to accelerate at a pace that has repeatedly exceeded expectations, driving growing demand across data centers, power generation, transmission infrastructure and digital connectivity assets. The intensity of this competition for energy and infrastructure is perhaps best illustrated by Alphabet’s $4.75 billion acquisition of Intersect Power, announced in December 20251, the first time a hyperscaler has moved to directly own a major renewable energy developer rather than rely on power purchase agreements.2 The deal is designed to give Google a team that can develop, build, and generate power directly alongside data centers, bypassing the lengthy timelines companies typically face when connecting new facilities to the electrical grid. This kind of vertical integration into the energy supply chain signals a meaningful escalation in how the largest technology companies are approaching the infrastructure buildout required to power AI at scale. While demand dynamics such as these often result in periods of overbuilding, the broader demand trends will undoubtedly produce a significant amount of productive, near-term infrastructure investment, coupled with some opportunistic investing in the future. For infrastructure investors, this distinction is important. Unlike sectors facing disruption risk from AI, infrastructure is critically necessary for the proliferation of AI, and therefore infrastructure assets are positioned as enabling components of the broader transformation. Forecasts for AI-related infrastructure spending have continued moving materially higher even after multiple upward revisions, underscoring the scale and persistence of anticipated demand growth. AI Capital Expenditures AI CapEx growth remains a dominant investment narrative with significant economic and market impact Source: Bloomberg Finance, L.P, S&P Global CapIQ. Data as of April 21, 2025. For illustrative purposes only. 1 Hyperscalers defined as Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle The implications extend well beyond digital infrastructure alone. Rising computing intensity is increasingly driving secondary demand for power generation, transmission upgrades, cooling systems and broader industrial supply chains required to support large-scale AI deployment. Pollock observed that the scale and speed of current AI-related capital expenditures may prove historically significant, particularly given the interconnected infrastructure systems required to support long-term computing demand. Infrastructure’s Positioning Remains Strong Infrastructure remains unusually well-positioned within the broader private markets landscape due to the simultaneous expansion of multiple secular demand drivers. Infrastructure continues to benefit from the emergence of entirely new categories of demand tied to digitalization, electrification, industrial modernization and AI-related development. Pollock noted that the unique correlation between continuing expansion of the infrastructure opportunity set, even as institutional appetite for the asset class has grown materially. Long-term capital demand remains supported by the essential nature of infrastructure assets, coupled with persistent funding gaps across all major segments of the market, including energy, transportation, grid modernization and digital infrastructure systems globally. U.S. Infrastructure Demand — Funding Gaps and AI Investment as % of GDP Source: American Society of Civil Engineers, KKR, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Bloomberg Finance, L.P. For illustrative purposes only. Over the coming decade, those funding requirements are expected to intersect with rising demand for power-intensive technologies, industrial electrification and continued modernization of aging infrastructure networks. The result is an environment in which infrastructure assets increasingly sit at the intersection of ongoing capital needs and secular economic transformation. Attractive Long-Term Infrastructure Supply/Demand Dynamics (2025–2040) Source: Global Infrastructure Outlook, World Bank, World Economic Forum, Human Development Report Office. For illustrative purposes only. Selectivity Is Becoming More Important Than Scale Despite the constructive long-term backdrop, the current market environment increasingly rewards underwriting discipline, asset selectivity and operational execution. In general, valuations across portions of both public and private markets remain elevated relative to prevailing financing conditions, limiting the likelihood that broad market exposure alone will drive returns over the coming decade. Instead, investors may increasingly need to rely on differentiated sourcing, operational value creation, and disciplined capital deployment when looking to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns. In that environment, scale alone may prove less important than the ability to navigate complexity, underwrite asset-level risk and access opportunities supported by long-duration secular demand drivers. Pollock emphasized that the current environment increasingly favors alpha generation over broad beta exposure, particularly as higher financing costs create greater dispersion across asset quality and execution capability. The combination of elevated valuations and ambitious earnings expectations continues to reinforce the importance of selectivity across both public and private markets. Equity Valuations and Earnings Growth Expectations Source: Bloomberg Finance, L.P. For illustrative purposes only. Past performance is not necessarily indicative of future results. The Next Constraint May Be Physical, Not Financial Looking ahead, one of the most important infrastructure investment themes may be the growing gap between capital availability and physical capacity. Pollock suggested that the primary constraints on AI-related infrastructure development have increasingly shifted away from financing availability and toward access to power, transmission capacity, land, permitting and community acceptance. Large-scale data center development, in particular, is beginning to place growing pressure on regional power grids, water systems and local infrastructure networks. Over time, those constraints may become increasingly economically relevant as developers and hyperscalers compete for limited access to critical infrastructure inputs. The result may be an environment in which physical scarcity — rather than capital scarcity — becomes one of the defining characteristics of next-generation digital infrastructure investing. A Constructive — but More Complex — Long-Term Outlook Despite continued macro uncertainty and geopolitical volatility, the long-term infrastructure backdrop remains supported by several converging secular forces, including AI adoption, electrification, digitalization and the ongoing need to modernize aging infrastructure systems globally. At the same time, the opportunity set is becoming increasingly complex. The next phase of infrastructure investing may depend less on identifying areas of demand — which appear abundant across many sectors — and more on determining where physical capacity can realistically scale alongside capital deployment. Pollock noted that infrastructure is increasingly positioned not simply as a defensive asset class, but as a foundational enabling layer of future economic growth. Assets located at the intersection of compute, power availability, connectivity and permitting capacity may ultimately define the next phase of infrastructure investment opportunity globally. title: Season 2 of Japan’s Chaotic Reality Series ‘Badly in Love’ Returns August 4
summary: Season 2 of Japan’s Chaotic Reality Series ‘Badly in Love’ Returns August 4
body_text: Japan’s first yankii dating reality show, where love lives on the edge and tempers flare, is back! Badly in Love Season 2 premieres worldwide on August 4, with 10 episodes released over three weeks, every Tuesday. This summer, a new lineup of rough-around-the-edges men and women clash, connect and search for romance. Season 1 of Badly in Love sparked buzz in Japan and beyond for its raw, unpredictable depiction of human emotions. The series reached #8 on the Netflix Global Top 10 (Non-English) Series list and appeared in the Top 10 rankings across Korea, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. Recently, the series won the Best Reality & Variety category at the KISF 2026 Global OTT Awards. Season 2 moves to a new setting in tropical Okinawa at the Badly in Love Marine Academy. Nine men and women from across Japan, all carrying complicated pasts, come together at the school, where a deeper, more intense drama unfolds. Returning as emcees are MEGUMI (who also serves as producer) and Nagano , who earned praise in Season 1 for voicing viewers' feelings as a self-professed reality romance first-timer. Joining them is Awich , a top artist from Okinawa with an international profile, marking her first-ever appearance as an emcee on a reality dating series. Beyond romance, Season 2 explores themes of regret and redemption, unbreakable bonds between companions, and the determination to start over. Watch as these men and women use love as a path to start anew. Badly in Love Season 2 premieres August 4, only on Netflix. Streaming Schedule: August 4 (Tue) — Episodes 1–4 August 11 (Tue) — Episodes 5–7 August 18 (Tue) — Episodes 8–10

title: Laser Cutting vs. Plasma Cutting: A Modern Guide
summary: Data proves that long-standing wisdom about cutting thick metal with fiber lasers is outdated.
body_text: Long-standing wisdom about cutting thick metal with fiber lasers has gradually become outdated. And an updated analysis of the relative capabilities of laser cutting and plasma cutting has become necessary. High-power fiber lasers – which are now available in powers exceeding 100 kilowatts — have flipped the script, challenging many long-held assumptions about cost, speed, and performance. Most critically, these higher power fiber laser cutters are no longer primarily limited to thin metals: they now consistently outperform plasma cutters at material thicknesses exceeding 2 inches (50 mm). This modernized guide provides a summary of the technological breakthroughs driving these changes and a data-driven comparison between fiber lasers and plasma cutters before answering the critical question: when is a laser cutter actually more economical than a plasma cutter? This information should help you decide if a laser cutter can deliver the performance, productivity, and ROI that satisfies your production requirements. Technological Advancements in High-Power Fiber Lasers The most significant advances have been in the pump diode technology that powers fiber laser sources. The output power achievable by a single emitter has risen several orders of magnitude, from a fraction of a watt to several dozen watts. Simultaneously, diode electrical efficiency has grown from around 20% to roughly 70%. These core advancements have driven down the cost-per-watt down by a factor of 100 while also increasing reliability and operational lifetime. System-Level Improvements for Thick Metal Cutting Raw laser power alone isn’t enough to cut thick metal efficiently. Progress in other cutting system components has also been essential. Improved beam delivery: Multi-mode fiber lasers, paired with cutting heads built specifically for high-power operation, now maintain tight beam focus over greater cutting depths. This is supplemented by optical techniques like beam wobble and dynamic focus modulation. Optimized assist gas delivery: Modern systems feature improved assist gas delivery that ejects molten material more efficiently during the cut. This is crucial for achieving clean cuts in thicker materials while maintaining high cutting speeds. Enhanced thermal management: High-power laser cutting generates significant heat. Advanced cooling, more efficient optics, and smarter system control allow fiber lasers to remain stable under continuous high thermal loads. Performance Analysis: Fiber Laser vs. Plasma Cutter It is already well-established that laser cutting offers significant advantages over plasma technology. Lasers deliver higher precision, produce a narrower and straighter kerf, and create a much smaller heat-affected zone (HAZ). Cleaner edges mean that laser-cut features are frequently weld-ready and do not require post-processing. Lasers can also accurately produce small holes with excellent roundness and little taper. This can save time and sometimes eliminates the need for secondary holemaking operations or drilling equipment. Fiber Laser Cutting: Faith in a Higher Power However, conventional wisdom has suggested that lasers are slower than plasma for cutting mild steel above 1 inch (25 mm) thick (and half that for stainless steel). This used to be (more or less) true. But it is no longer the case. To see how that has changed with the emergence of widely available high-power fiber lasers, let’s review some actual (and more current) cutting data. The graphs above chart cutting speed relative to material thickness, comparing best-in-class fiber laser and plasma cutting technology. These plots for mild steel and stainless steel show that high-power fiber lasers almost always cut at higher rates than plasma cutters for materials from 10 mm to 40 mm thick. Even on 40 mm thick material, a 60 kW laser cuts mild steel about 2.5X faster than a 460 A plasma cutter. For stainless steel of the same thickness, the advantage increases to 3.2X faster. The data shows that plasma cutters only perform better than fiber lasers when laser power is decreased to 30 kW or lower. And only when cutting thicker sections. Understanding Assist Gas The fastest and cleanest way to cut steel with a fiber laser is using a mixed assist gas (nitrogen with a small amount of oxygen). Every cutting test represented on the charts above where laser outperformed plasma used mixed assist gas. However, once a sufficiently low laser power-to-thickness ratio is reached, it becomes necessary to switch to pure oxygen. Oxygen assist gas prevents the laser cutting process from stalling but at a necessarily lower rate and while producing a lower quality edge. Pure oxygen was required in the tests where laser cutting performed worse than plasma cutting. Fortunately, this problem is completely eliminated when using a more powerful laser. When using a laser in the 40 kW or higher power range, mixed assist gas is ideal for cutting all but the thickest metals (well in excess of 40 mm). Ultimately, this means that fiber lasers of 40 kW and above cut steel faster than plasma – often by a very significant factor – for the vast majority of cutting applications. And they accomplish this while also delivering cleaner, straighter edges with minimal dross. ROI Analysis: When Does a Fiber Laser Make Sense? High-power fiber lasers outperform plasma cutters in speed, quality, and consistency, but they also cost more to purchase. Fortunately, their higher throughput can quickly earn back that extra capital expense. Most operating costs – amortization, labor, overhead, and maintenance – are tied to owning and operating the system, not how fast it cuts. Electricity and other consumables do increase with system power and use, but don’t scale in proportion to the extra throughput. So, if laser and plasma cutters cost roughly the same to operate over a month (which they do), the machine that produces more output over that time will always be the more economical one. A Cost and Output Example Let’s compare a 40 kW fiber laser to a 300 A plasma cutter using the data from earlier. The 40 kW fiber laser cuts 20 mm thick mild steel at approximately 8 m/min. At full utilization, it can make about 38,000 meters of cuts per month . The 300 A plasma cutter works at roughly half that speed, yielding about 19,000 meters in the same period . We can accurately estimate that both systems cost about $20,000 per month to operate at these utilization levels. If the product requirement is approximately 38,000 meters, one laser cutter meets the demand. Achieving the same output with plasma cutting requires two machines, doubling the monthly operating cost to $40,000 . If the single laser costs $400,000 more to purchase than the two plasma cutters, that $20,000 in monthly savings makes up the price difference in just 20 months. Is a High-Power Fiber Laser Cutting Machine Right for You? Laser cutting delivers the best value and fastest ROI under specific conditions. Considering investing in a high-power fiber laser if your operation involves: High utilization: The machine is kept busy enough for throughput-driven savings to accumulate quickly. Clean edge requirements: Reduced (or eliminated) post-processing turns directly into labor and equipment savings. Welded assemblies: Weld-ready laser edges cut prep time and improve downstream flow. Fine features: Lasers can create small holes and tight contours in a single operation. Floor space is limited: One high-power laser can replace multiple plasma cutters and shrink the required footprint. Part geometry is complex: Intricate shapes, tight radii, and internal features favor laser cutting over plasma every time. Getting Started with a Laser Cutting Solution As fiber laser technology continues to advance and the capabilities of laser machines increase, deciding between a laser cutter and a plasma cutter becomes more complicated. For many fabricators and manufacturers, lasers have become an ideal tool for metal cutting. For others, plasma cutting remains more practical. Talk to one of our laser cutting experts to see what kind of results and ROI you can expect in your application. title: GetAccept welcomes Jon Buss as Non-Executive Director to the GetAccept Board
summary: GetAccept, the category leader within the Digital Sales Room space, is pleased to announce the appointment of Jon Buss as a Non-Executive Director (NED) to its board.
body_text: Malmö, July 3, 2023 — GetAccept, the category leader within the Digital Sales Room space, is pleased to announce the appointment of Jon Buss as a Non-Executive Director (NED) to its board. Jon brings a wealth of experience and a strong background in go-to-market (GTM) strategies, operational expertise, and revenue growth. His appointment is expected to significantly enhance the company's growth journey and further support its management team. Jon Buss has an impressive track record of driving growth and success across various global organizations. He currently serves as Managing Director at Incode Technologies, a pioneer in the identity verification and biometric authentication industry. Jon has over 25 years of sales and general management leadership experience, primarily in the technology industry, with global companies at all stages of growth. Before joining Incode, Jon was Managing Director and EVP at Yext, a $400M revenue NYSE-listed technology company, where he led the EMEA business from $2M to $85M ARR. He’s also held international executive leadership roles at Criteo, Experian, Dun & Bradstreet, and Computacentre. In addition to his executive roles, Jon Buss has served as a NED and advisor to several organizations. He is currently an Advisor at Roam, an all-in-one Cloud HQ designed to unite distributed companies, and an Investor & Advisor at Kore Labs, a platform for creating and managing financial products. Furthermore, Jon sat as a NED at BREVO (formally SENDINBLUE), an all-in-one marketing platform that grew rapidly during his time on the board from 2018 to 2021. Commenting on his appointment, Jon Buss said, "GetAccept is a dynamic and innovative company well-positioned for remarkable growth. I am thrilled to join the board and work closely with the CEO, management team, and my fellow directors to accelerate the company's success. With my experience in driving revenue growth and go-to-market strategies, I look forward to contributing to GetAccept's expansion and helping them achieve new heights." GetAccept's CEO and Co-founder, Samir Smajic, is excited about Jon Buss joining the board, "We are thrilled to have Jon Buss on board! His deep expertise in go-to-market strategies and execution will be invaluable as we continue our growth journey. We believe Jon's addition to our already strong team will enable us to reach new levels of success and drive innovation in our industry." About GetAccept GetAccept was founded in 2015 by Swedish entrepreneurs and Y Combinator alumni to bridge the gap between outdated sales processes and bad buyer experiences. As the creator and frontrunner of the Digital Sales Room category, GetAccept empowers revenue teams to increase their win rates by engaging and understanding buyers from opportunity to signed deal. Seamless integrations with CRMs like Salesforce, HubSpot, and Microsoft Dynamics allow sellers to collaborate and offer the best buyer experience while shortening sales cycles. Voted as the 11th best sales product of 2023 by G2 Best Software Awards , the platform serves 40,000+ users across 4,000+ enterprises within 60+ countries. GetAccept is headquartered in Malmö, Sweden, with 200+ employees across the US, Sweden, United Kingdom, France, Norway, and Denmark. To learn more, visit www.getaccept.com Media Contact: Frida Ahrenby Chief Marketing Officer at GetAccept frida.ahrenby@getaccept.com Phone +46 73 666 11 42 About the author GetAccept GetAccept is a Digital Sales Room platform trusted by more than 5000 revenue teams to help reps spend more time selling and less time on admin. We bring static sales content and scattered communication into one shared space where every stakeholder can access the latest content, timelines, and context throughout the whole sales cycle. And with purpose-built AI that truly understands the context of your deals, creating and updating personalized content takes minutes. Native integrations with popular CRMs let reps work with their existing tools, while making sure activity is automatically synced and updated everywhere it matters. In short – we help sales teams work smart, close faster, and win more. LinkedIn View all posts

title: AI Time Tracking Software for Lawyers: 10 Best Tools & Pricing (2026)
summary: Compare the 10 best AI time tracking tools for lawyers in July 2026, with pricing, features, and OCG compliance details for every firm size.
body_text: AI Summary 10 tools compared: PointOne, Ajax, Laurel, Billables AI, Clio Duo, BigHand SmartTime, Intapp Time, Tempello, WiseTime, and Memtime. Where each stands out: PointOne for narrative quality and accurate matter attribution; Ajax for the most granular capture detail; Billables AI for value at the small-firm end. Capability drives price: the most advanced AI-native tools write client-ready narratives and enforce billing compliance, and sit at the custom/premium end (PointOne, Ajax, Laurel, BigHand, Intapp); tools that only log activity cost less (Memtime, WiseTime) but leave the writing to you. How to choose: shortlist two, run a two-week pilot on real matters, and compare both recovered billable time and the quality of the generated narratives. Top AI time tracking tools for lawyers in 2026 The 2026 landscape of legal timekeeping features a range of specialized platforms tailored to different firm sizes, operational requirements, and existing software ecosystems. Tool Automation level Compliance Capabilities Best for PointOne Yes, fully automated with AI timers, retrocapture, and autocapture modes High Mid-size to large law firms. Ajax Yes Limited Solos and small law firms. Laurel Yes Medium Accounting firms. Billables.ai Yes No Solo and boutique law firms. Clio Duo Suggestions Limited Solo and boutique law firms. BigHand SmartTime Yes Approval workflow Large firms. Intapp Time No Limited Large firms on legacy systems. Lawgro MagicTime Yes Limited Solo and boutique law firms. WiseTime Partially No Solo and boutique law firms. Memtime No, rule-based entry automation only No Solo and boutique law firms. PointOne PointOne Time captures work passively across email, documents, calls, and web activity, then generates entries that already match firm policy and client OCGs . Designed specifically for complex legal billing environments, the platform layers on top of Aderant, Clio, Elite 3E, SurePoint, and QuickBooks, so firms keep their existing billing system without requiring a disruptive rip-and-replace implementation. By turning passive work data into operational intelligence, PointOne enables finance teams to understand utilization and margins while eliminating the friction of manual time entry for attorneys. Ajax Ajax reads on-screen content to build elaborate time entries, capturing across many applications without configuring a separate integration for each one. Reviewers note that this screen-based approach produces granular narratives, but it sits at a premium price point and requires a desktop installation for every attorney. It appeals most to firms that rank maximum entry detail above all else, while some compliance and IT teams weigh the trade-offs of a screen-reading approach against integration-based alternatives. Laurel Positioned as a "time intelligence" platform rather than a simple tracker, Laurel captures work activity and layers on compliance review , automated billing-code assignment, and profitability analytics. Analysts note it is among the most heavily funded vendors in the category and has focused largely on accounting firms in recent years, which broadens its scope beyond purely legal workflows. Billables.ai For practices seeking automated tracking without enterprise-level complexity, Billables.ai provides a streamlined solution. Market evaluations highlight Billables.ai as an affordable passive capture tool serving solo to boutique law firms. The software connects to daily work tools like Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Zoom via API integrations and uses AI to categorize tasks by client and matter with auto-generated narratives. While it may lack the deep OCG compliance enforcement found in enterprise platforms, its straightforward implementation and cost-effective pricing structure make it an accessible entry point for small firms aiming looking to move off of traditional manual timers. Clio Duo Operating within the broader Clio Manage ecosystem, Clio Duo functions as an intelligent assistant for legal professionals. Industry analysts describe Clio Duo as an active logging tool ideal for fixing poor billing narratives . Rather than passively monitoring background activity, it prompts users to refine and expand their manual entries using generative AI. This approach ensures that time records meet the stringent requirements of corporate clients, making it a strong option for solo practitioners and small firms already utilizing Clio's practice management infrastructure. BigHand SmartTime BigHand SmartTime offers a robust time capture solution tailored for large, global law firms. The platform combines active timers with passive activity monitoring to create a comprehensive daily timesheet. Its strength lies in its enterprise-grade analytics and reporting capabilities, which provide firm leadership with granular visibility into timekeeper performance and missing time. The system integrates deeply with legacy financial systems, though its interface and deployment process reflect its focus on large-scale, complex organizational structures. Intapp Time Intapp Time is an established enterprise timekeeping product now adding AI capabilities on top of its existing foundation. Its strength is deep integration with large-firm financial and practice systems, making it a familiar option for firms already invested in legacy infrastructure. Because its AI features are layered onto an older architecture, firms often evaluate it against newer AI-native platforms when automated narratives and matter accuracy are the priority. Lawgro MagicTime Lawgro MagicTime is an AI-based automated timekeeping tool built specifically for lawyers. It captures billable minutes in the background across the applications attorneys use — email, Word, court websites, legal research tools — then builds a timesheet that users review and file in a few clicks. Its AI categorizes captured activity and tags it to the correct client and matter, with customizable rules controlling what gets captured. MagicTime integrates with practice management platforms like Clio, PracticePanther, and Rocket Matter, making it a natural fit for solo and small firms already running on those systems. Tempello Tempello focuses on simplifying the time capture process through an intuitive, minimalist interface. It connects to Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, matches each email to the correct matter using metadata and AI, and automatically creates time entries in Clio or MyCase — no timers and no desktop monitoring. Pricing is per billable email processed rather than per seat, which appeals to small firms with fluctuating headcount. Because it captures email activity only, it serves as a targeted supplement for firms whose missed time hides in their inboxes, rather than a comprehensive capture or billing compliance engine. WiseTime WiseTime runs autonomously in the background, auto-tagging activity to the correct matter and refining its suggestions over time. It recently added AI narrative summaries, but reviewers characterize it as an activity tracker that still leaves attorneys to finalize entries rather than a tool that writes complete, client-ready narratives. Its lower price and strong privacy controls suit budget-conscious firms comfortable with a lighter, previous-generation approach. Memtime Memtime records computer activity and presents it as a private, local timeline for reconstructing timesheets, with all data stored on the user's own device. Users create their own entries from the timeline, optionally assisted by rule-based automation, but the tool is not legal-specific and does not attribute matters or write narratives — it functions as a memory aid rather than a billing tool. Its offline architecture and low price make it attractive for privacy-strict or cost-sensitive users, including non-legal professionals who bill by the hour. The three ways these tools differ How they capture work — screen-based, app/metadata integration, or simple activity logging. Whether they write the entry — AI-native tools draft the narrative and matter; trackers only log activity. Compliance depth — whether they enforce Outside Counsel Guidelines and UTBMS codes at entry, and push into billing systems (Aderant, Elite 3E, Clio, SurePoint). Pricing tiers $12–$40/user/mo: Memtime, WiseTime. Cheapest because they do not write complete, client-ready entries. $39–$99/user/mo: Billables AI. Most affordable tool that writes entries. $149/user/mo: Clio Manage AI, bundled in Clio Complete. Custom / enterprise: PointOne, Ajax, Laurel, BigHand, Intapp Time. Priced on firm size, seats, and platform scope. Most enterprise vendors quote custom pricing. Compare price against billable hours recovered: firms lose an estimated 10–20% of billable time to manual entry. Your AI-powered firm starts here Book a demo Your AI-powered firm starts here Book a demo Your AI-powered firm starts here Book a demo FAQs about AI time tracking for lawyers How much does AI time tracking software cost? It ranges from about $12/user/month for a basic activity logger to custom enterprise pricing. Tools that write full time entries generally start around $40/user/month. Are cheaper AI timekeeping tools worth it? The lowest-priced options, like Memtime (~$12/user/month), are activity logs or memory aids — they do not write time entries or attribute work to the right matter. Tools with genuinely advanced AI that draft client-ready narratives and assign entries to the correct matter cost more, but recover far more billable time. For most firms the value is in AI quality, not the lowest sticker price. What makes an AI timekeeping tool high quality? The quality of the AI itself — how accurately it attributes work to the correct client and matter, and how well-written and compliant its generated narratives are. The most advanced platforms produce client-ready entries that need little editing and pass billing review the first time, which is what drives real billable-hour recovery. What is the difference between AI time tacking tools? Three things: how they capture work (screen, metadata, or activity log), whether they write complete entries or just log activity, and how deeply they enforce billing compliance. Do these tools integrate with legal billing systems? The leading tools integrate with Aderant, Elite 3E, Clio, and SurePoint. Integration depth varies by vendor.

title: Cumplimiento LFPIORPI en México: Obligaciones, Umbrales y Sanciones, Guía 2026
summary: La reforma 2025 a la Ley Antilavado ahora exige mecanismos automatizados de monitoreo. Tu dirección general quiere crecer — la regulación exige cumplir. Esta guía desglosa qué te toca hacer, cuánto cuesta no hacerlo y dónde el proceso de cumplimiento está frenando tu cierre de clientes.
body_text: Cumplimiento LFPIORPI en México: Obligaciones, Umbrales y Sanciones, Guía 2026 La reforma 2025 a la Ley Antilavado ahora exige mecanismos automatizados de monitoreo. Tu dirección general quiere crecer — la regulación exige cumplir. Esta guía desglosa qué te toca hacer, cuánto cuesta no hacerlo y dónde el proceso de cumplimiento está frenando tu cierre de clientes. Qué cambió: la Reforma LFPIORPI 2025 y la obligación de automatizar Desde julio de 2025, la reforma a la LFPIORPI introdujo un cambio estructural que muchas empresas aún no dimensionan. El nuevo Artículo 18, Fracción X, establece que todo sujeto obligado debe contar con mecanismos automatizados que permitan el monitoreo permanente de operaciones para identificar transacciones fuera del perfil del cliente y dar seguimiento intensificado a Personas Políticamente Expuestas (PEPs) y clientes de alto riesgo. Automatizar ya no es una decisión de eficiencia operativa. Es un requisito legal. Adicionalmente, la reforma elevó el periodo de conservación documental de 5 a 10 años, amplió las actividades vulnerables (incluyendo la nueva Fracción V Bis para desarrollo inmobiliario) y reforzó el enfoque basado en riesgos (EBR) como obligación explícita. Para dirección general, esto significa que el dilema entre crecimiento y cumplimiento se agudizó: hay más obligaciones, más documentación, más monitoreo — y ahora la ley exige que parte de eso esté automatizado. Obligaciones LFPIORPI: las cuatro etapas del ciclo de cumplimiento que impactan tu funnel de ventas Todo sujeto obligado debe ejecutar un ciclo de cumplimiento que se repite con cada cliente y cada transacción relevante. Estos son los cuatro bloques que directamente impactan el tiempo de cierre comercial: Integración del expediente KYC/KYB: qué documentos exige la ley Antes de transaccionar, hay que recabar identificaciones oficiales vigentes (INE, pasaporte, cédula profesional), actas constitutivas, poderes notariales, constancias de situación fiscal y documentación del Beneficiario Controlador. Para personas morales con estructuras de holding, esto implica rastrear cadenas de propiedad hasta llegar a las personas físicas reales — extrayendo razón social, RFC, objeto social, régimen de capital, accionistas con porcentaje de participación, consejo de administración y datos notariales de cada eslabón. Un solo expediente corporativo puede requerir el análisis de 15 a 30 documentos de más de 15 tipos distintos. Impacto en ventas: Este es el momento donde el prospecto tiene máxima intención de compra y mínima paciencia para procesos administrativos. Cada documento adicional es fricción. Cada día que tarda el expediente es una oportunidad para que busque alternativa. ‍ Impacto en proceso de ventas LFPIORPI Validación documental y dictaminación legal de personas morales: el cuello de botella oculto No basta con recibir documentos. La normativa exige cotejar originales, verificar vigencia de identificaciones, confirmar facultades legales en poderes notariales (tipo de poder, alcance, limitaciones, revocaciones, vigencia) y validar la congruencia entre actas constitutivas y la estructura declarada. Un poder revocado que no se detectó o un acta con modificaciones no reflejadas invalida todo el expediente. Impacto en ventas: Un analista experimentado toma entre 2 y 5 minutos por documento simple (identificaciones, constancias), pero hasta 40 minutos por acta constitutiva — el documento más denso del expediente. Con prospectos corporativos de dos o tres niveles de holding, el análisis completo puede consumir un día entero. El equipo comercial queda en espera. Consultas a fuentes oficiales y monitoreo PLD/FT Cada prospecto y beneficiario controlador debe validarse contra fuentes gubernamentales y cruzarse contra listas de personas bloqueadas: ‍ Consultas a fuentes oficiales y monitoreo PLD/FT Fuente oficial Qué valida Input requerido SIGER 2.0 (32 estados) Actas inscritas, poderes vigentes, accionistas, estado de la empresa RFC o Folio Mercantil SAT Situación fiscal, e.firma, régimen fiscal, domicilio fiscal RFC Renapo Validación de CURP, datos demográficos CURP Lista Nominal INE Vigencia de credencial de elector Datos del INE Listas PLD (OFAC, ONU, nacionales) Personas bloqueadas y sanciones Nombre / RFC ‍ Impacto en ventas: Consultas manuales a múltiples portales agregan días al proceso. Y ahora la ley exige que este monitoreo sea continuo y con mecanismos automatizados — no es opcional. Reporte periódico de Avisos al SAT Los Avisos deben enviarse en formato XML antes del día 17 del mes siguiente, incluyendo "Informes en Ceros" para periodos inactivos. ‍ Tabla de umbrales LFPIORPI por Actividad Vulnerable: cuándo se detona cada obligación Los umbrales (en UMAs; 2026: 1 UMA ≈ $113.14 MXN) determinan dos momentos: cuándo integrar el expediente completo ("Identificación") y cuándo reportar al SAT ("Aviso"). El mecanismo de acumulación exige sumar operaciones del mismo cliente durante 6 meses. ‍ Umbrales LFPIORPI por Actividad Vulnerable Los umbrales determinan cuándo integrar el expediente completo (Identificación) y cuándo reportar al SAT (Aviso). 2026: 1 UMA ≈ $113.14 MXN. Acumulación: 6 meses por cliente. V Bis) Siempre 8,025 UMAs (~$907K) "Siempre" = no hay monto mínimo. La obligación aplica desde la primera operación. ‍ Sanciones LFPIORPI: la matriz de consecuencias que debe conocer dirección general El diseño sancionatorio castiga la omisión procesal con mayor dureza que el impacto fiscal: ‍ Sanciones LFPIORPI: matriz de consecuencias Tipo de falla Sanción económica Consecuencia penal Omisión de Avisos 10,000–65,000 UMAs ($1.1M–$7.3M MXN) o 10–100% del valor de la operación (la mayor) — Avisos tardíos o con errores 200–2,000 UMAs ($22K–$226K MXN) — Falsificación o manipulación Cierre de operaciones y bloqueo Prisión de 2 a 8 años No contar con mecanismos automatizados REFORMA 2025 Pendiente de reglamentación por SHCP — ‍ El Representante Encargado de Cumplimiento (Art. 20) asume la firma y responsabilidad de los reportes. Pero si la empresa no demuestra Manual de Cumplimiento interno ni resguardo de expedientes por 10 años (antes eran 5), la responsabilidad escala al Consejo de Administración. ‍ Dónde se rompe el funnel de ventas: tres métricas de cumplimiento que impactan revenue La mayoría de las empresas en Actividades Vulnerables no tienen visibilidad sobre cuánto negocio pierden por su proceso de cumplimiento: ‍ Métricas de cumplimiento que impactan revenue Métrica Proceso manual Proceso automatizado Delta Costo por expediente corporativo >$15,000 MXN Fracción del costo 70–80% reducción Tiempo de onboarding regulatorio 5–15 días hábiles 1–3 días 25–50% reducción desde mes 1 Documentos solicitados al cliente P Física: 3-5 P Moral: 10-15 por expediente Solo los no verificables en fuentes oficiales Hasta 80% menos Tasa de abandono por complejidad Alta (no se mide) Baja (checklist dinámico en tiempo real) Directamente ligada a revenue ‍ La tasa de abandono por complejidad documental es la métrica más importante y la más cara. Prospectos que nunca terminan de entregar los documentos requeridos. No es que no quieran comprar — es que el proceso los expulsa. ‍ Impacto en funnel de ventas Qué significa la Reforma 2025 para tu estrategia de crecimiento La regulación LFPIORPI no va a simplificarse. La reforma de julio 2025 marcó la dirección: más obligaciones, plazos más largos de conservación, y — por primera vez — la exigencia legal de contar con mecanismos automatizados de monitoreo . El dilema para dirección general es real: no puedes frenar el crecimiento para cumplir, ni aceptar riesgo regulatorio para crecer. Pero es un falso dilema si el proceso está bien diseñado. Empresas como Clara, Actinver, Finsus y Bepensa ya procesan sus expedientes con plataformas de automatización documental especializadas, logrando precisión superior al 99% en extracción de datos y reduciendo el onboarding de semanas a días — cumpliendo con la ley sin frenar la operación comercial. La pregunta no es si automatizar. Desde julio de 2025, la ley lo exige. La pregunta es cuánto revenue estás dejando en la mesa mientras decides cómo implementarlo. ‍

title: Getting Started with Gen AI in Insurance: Benefits and Use Cases
summary: Gen AI has the potential to reshape the insurance value chain, enhancing productivity and delivering better customer experiences.
body_text: Underwriting. Generative AI can assist underwriters in evaluating potential risks by analyzing vast amounts of data, including historical claims, customer information, and external factors to generate risk profiles and recommend appropriate coverage levels, helping underwriters make more informed decisions quickly. Claims processing and fraud detection. Generative AI can streamline the claims process by automating the assessment of claims documents. It can extract relevant information from documents, summarize claims histories, and identify potential inconsistencies or fraudulent claims based on patterns and anomalies in the data. Quote and policy generation. Generative AI can automate the generation of insurance quotes, policies, and associated documentation. It can create quotes, policy documents, invoices, and certificates based on predefined templates and customer information, reducing manual administrative tasks. Customer support and engagement. AI-powered chatbots reduce the workload on human agents and provide 24/7 customer support to offer immediate answers to policy, coverage, and claims questions. Generative AI can also automate personalized communication with policyholders by sending reminders for premium payments, providing policy updates, and delivering relevant content to enhance customer engagement and retention. Customer upsell/cross-sell opportunities. Generative AI can analyze customer data and preferences to recommend tailored insurance products. By understanding customer needs and risk profiles, insurers can offer personalized coverage options, increasing the likelihood of upselling or cross-selling additional policies. The versatility of generative AI in the insurance industry is immense, and its power cannot be overstated. But there’s a big gap between knowing what AI can be used for and operationalizing it in your organization. That’s where strategic technology partners can help.

title: Raised $1.6M to build satellite based infrastructure monitoring powered by AI & InSAR
body_text: We are thrilled to report that we have closed a $1.6 million pre-seed investment to revolutionize the way ground motion data is collected and analyzed by integrating satellite-based sensors with ground sensor networks and using artificial intelligence to help interpret risk levels. In addition to the financing, we secured an additional non-dilutive investment of $600,000 in the last year from institutions such as the Canadian space agency, SDTC, and NRC IRAP. We believe that infrastructure managers, such as engineers and maintenance managers, experience safety risks, costly repairs, and disruptions to operations when inaccurate ground motion data is collected and analyzed, particularly in areas with limited ground sensor networks or difficult terrain, because of the limited availability and accuracy of ground motion data. Alleviating that pain by providing a solution that integrates satellite data, IoT, and AI to accurately and comprehensively assess the physical integrity of critical structures, as well as monitor subsidence risks, would allow them to make informed engineering and maintenance decisions and avoid potential hazards, leading to safer and more efficient operations. We are thrilled to have some of the best investors in the round, including Y Combinator, ParticleX, Sustainable Development Technology Canada, Berg, Emeles, UVP, and strategic mining angel investors. We plan to drive product development, convert existing proof of ideas, and secure customers during the next 12 months.
